_role: Labelled routing cases for the Sovereign System One evaluator (SSO contract §8.5) and for backend-vs-backend parity between TypeSafe Jev and the local laya façade. Consumed by system-one-eval (Rust) and by tests/system-one/routing-corpus.test.mjs (JS validation). Schema and honest limitations: tests/system-one/README.md.

_schema.prompt: A user turn, as a user would actually type it. Always >= 24 chars so the router's min_prompt_chars skip never fires on a case.
_schema.expected_skill: A directory name under the skills tree that survives loadCandidates(), or the literal "none".
_schema.rationale: Why that label and not the nearest wrong one. A label without a stated reason is an opinion.
_schema.late_discriminative: true when the expected skill's rubric is longer than 48 tokens AND its first when-to-use / when-NOT-to-use boundary clause begins after the 48-token cut, so laya's unconditional per-option truncation (SSO contract §10.1) would amputate the clause that makes the label correct. Computed, not judged: 48 tokens taken as 192 chars from the estate's own datum (median 461-char description ≈ 115 tokens), first boundary clause located by the marker regex recorded in tests/system-one/README.md. An estimate of a cut, not a tokenisation of it — the façade reports the real compressed token count in sso.shortlisted. system-one-eval reports this subgroup separately; it is never excluded from the headline number.

_provenance.items-json-tier-A: Verbatim from skills/system-one/scripts/items.json tier A — prompts authored in earlier sessions, before this corpus and by a different task. The only genuinely independent prompts here.
_provenance.directory-derived: Written from the 'When to Choose' / 'NOT for' columns of skills/SKILL-DIRECTORY.md, which is authored separately from the frontmatter `description` the router actually scores. Independent of the text under test, but not of this repo.
_provenance.log-shaped: Conversational turns written to match the SHAPE of the 66 `none` picks and 13 short-prompt skips in ~/.claude/skill-route.jsonl. The log records outcomes, never prompt text, so nothing here is a recovered user turn.

cases.prompt: Nobody here can explain how this repo fits together any more. I want the whole thing mapped in diagrams, in the repo, checked in, so the next person can read it — and I want to know what's dodgy in it while you're at it.
cases.rationale: Whole-repo diagram corpus, checked in, with an audit of what is wrong — diagrams-as-code's stated scope against mermaid-diagrams (a single diagram) and diagram-design (a published visual).

cases.prompt: There's a docs/diagrams tree in here from a few months ago. Is any of it still true? We've shipped a lot since.
cases.rationale: Re-verifying an existing docs/diagrams tree against HEAD is named explicitly in the skill's when-to-choose.

cases.prompt: We're handing this codebase to a client next week. Use the diagram corpus in docs/diagrams to build them something they can actually read, and add a couple of diagrams for the bits it doesn't cover.
cases.rationale: Known-ambiguous: the audience-facing half is explainer's. items.json records this as a genuine dual-skill request; kept as a deliberate hard case, and a pick of `explainer` should be read as a near-miss, not a failure.

cases.prompt: Put a CI gate on our diagrams so this stops rotting. The runner only checks out this one repo, and half our diagrams cite the sibling repos.
cases.rationale: The gate binary with --worktree-citations is the skill's own, and no CI skill covers diagram citation checking.

cases.prompt: We just finished a build sprint on ~/workspace/co-created/the target repository for a client. Before I hand it over I need it explained properly to three kinds of people: the marketing users, whoever picks up the code next, and their CTO who is not that technical. Can you set that up?
cases.rationale: Three-audience handover of a repo to people who did not build it is explainer's headline case.

cases.prompt: write me a repo primer for the agentbox management-api so an agent can actually answer questions about it from source, plus a short page for humans
cases.rationale: "Repo primer" is a stated trigger; the docs-bundle delivery reference covers the agent-readable corpus.

cases.prompt: explain what this product does to my CEO in a page, she'll ask what it costs and what could go wrong
cases.rationale: "Explain this to the CEO" is quoted verbatim in the directory's when-to-choose column.

cases.prompt: Build an explainer site for the target repository for an experienced engineer who did not write it and is wary of AI-generated filler. Explain the code as it stands, why it is shaped that way, and where to look. Don't narrate how the site was made.
cases.rationale: Instructional microsite (the former repo-education) is now an explainer delivery reference, so the deprecated skill must not be picked.

cases.prompt: Start the executive explainer for ~/workspace/co-created/the target repository for a technically literate CEO or investor, following walkthroughs/executive/teaching-contract.md. Produce only this slice: chapters 1 and 2 as Markdown with front matter; one diagram of request to publication; two or three labelled screenshots; one 30 to 60 second captioned clip with local narration; and run the gates on each.
cases.rationale: Multi-artefact but explainer owns the arc and hands the clip to codebase-video; a pick of codebase-video is a near-miss on the hand-off, not a different intent.

cases.prompt: I need one sequence diagram of the auth handshake to drop into the README, as a .mmd file we can version.
cases.rationale: A single version-controlled .mmd is mermaid-diagrams; diagrams-as-code explicitly excludes the single-diagram case.

cases.prompt: We're publishing a blog post about our architecture next week and the diagram needs to look like it belongs in a magazine — branded, dark mode, self-contained SVG.
cases.rationale: Editorial, branded, shared-publicly output is diagram-design's boundary against mermaid-diagrams.

cases.prompt: Map our whole VPC and the on-prem racks as one isometric infrastructure picture I can put in the runbook.
cases.rationale: Isometric network/infrastructure topology is fossflow's sole stated niche inside the diagram family.

cases.prompt: Plot where container orchestration sits on the evolution axis against our competitors so I can argue build versus buy to the board.
cases.rationale: Evolution axis and competitive positioning name Wardley mapping; report-builder can render one but the intent is the strategic analysis.

cases.prompt: Which of the browser tools should I be using for this job? I genuinely don't know where to start.
cases.rationale: The meta-skill's entire purpose is the "unsure which browser tool" turn; picking a concrete browser skill here is the error it exists to prevent.

cases.prompt: Take a screenshot of the staging login page and fill in the demo credentials for me.
cases.rationale: Navigate/screenshot/form-fill via the sidecar is `browser`; `playwright` is superseded and must never be offered at runtime. | RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-09-21: was `browser`. The `browser` rubric itself states "for a browser TASK choose `browser-automation`, not this; choose this only when the sidecar connection details themselves are the subject". A screenshot-and-fill request is a browser task. Two independent judges (openjev 4B cross-encoder, TypeSafe Jev at 0.98) both chose browser-automation; the original label rewarded lexical overlap with the `browser` entry.

cases.prompt: I've got forty tabs open in my logged-in Chrome and I want the console errors out of one of them without restarting the browser.
cases.rationale: Inspecting already-open, logged-in tabs is chrome-cdp's stated boundary against launching a fresh browser session.

cases.prompt: Scrape the product listings off this supplier site — it's behind Cloudflare Turnstile and rate-limits hard.
cases.rationale: Anti-bot bypass and spidering is scrapling, not general browser automation.

cases.prompt: Search the web for what's been published on HNSW recall degradation under bulk updates. I want dense page extracts to ground on, not somebody's synthesis.
cases.rationale: Dense extracts for LLM grounding and default-first web search is ceramic-search; perplexity-research is the synthesised-answer neighbour.

cases.prompt: Get me the authoritative government and academic sources on UK grid connection queue reform, filtered to gov and ac domains, with a synthesised answer.
cases.rationale: Authoritative primary sources with domain filters and a synthesised answer is perplexity-research's stated second-choice role.

cases.prompt: This goes into a client filing, so every citation has to be verifiable and archived. Restrict the search to SEC EDGAR and court records and audit the bibliography afterwards.
cases.rationale: Reputation-attached work with trusted-domain lenses and citation integrity tooling is web-researcher's explicit boundary against the two search skills.

cases.prompt: Write me a cited research brief on solid-state battery manufacturing that will survive a hostile reviewer picking at the sources.
cases.rationale: Multi-source cited brief with integrity gates is deep-research; the single-engine search skills are its tools, not the intent.

cases.prompt: Summarise these three articles and the conference talk on YouTube, and drop the note links into my vault.
cases.rationale: URL and YouTube summarisation with vault note links is web-summary; gemini-url-context is the nearest neighbour but has no vault step.

cases.prompt: Review PR #482 before I merge it — I want the security and performance problems called out.
cases.rationale: PR review is the one GitHub skill whose scope is reviewing rather than automating.

cases.prompt: Our release process is manual and error-prone. Automate the versioning, the changelog and the rollback path.
cases.rationale: Versioning, changelog and rollback are release management, not workflow authoring.

cases.prompt: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the test suite on every push to main and caches the cargo registry.
cases.rationale: Authoring an Actions pipeline is workflow-automation's sole scope.

cases.prompt: What does our knowledge graph actually say about the Loom façade? Ground the answer in the KG rather than guessing from memory.
cases.rationale: "What does our KG say about X" at inference time is ontology-augment; the other two ontology skills build and enrich schemas.

cases.prompt: Build a fresh OWL2 schema out of the vault pages for the podcast domain and export it as TTL for WebVOWL.
cases.rationale: Creating a new schema from the vault corpus is ontology-core, not enrichment of an existing dataset.

cases.prompt: We have an existing ontology dataset with gaps. Validate it and fill in the missing properties before we regenerate the TTL.
cases.rationale: Validation and enrichment of existing ontology data is the stated split from ontology-core.

cases.prompt: Make the dashboard bolder — the type is timid and the hierarchy reads flat. One pass, just that.
cases.rationale: "Make it bolder / fix the type" is design-audit's inferred-intent refinement lens, quoted in the directory.

cases.prompt: Generate a landing page prototype from our DESIGN.md brand spec and put it through the critique gate.
cases.rationale: Producing an artefact from a brand spec through the critique gate is open-design; design-audit reviews what already exists.

cases.prompt: I haven't picked a palette or a font pairing yet and I'd like to see the options before we lock a brand.
cases.rationale: Discovery and inspiration before a brand spec exists is explicitly upstream of open-design.

cases.prompt: Batch-transcode this directory of 4K MOV files to H.264 MP4 with CUDA acceleration, two-pass.
cases.rationale: Mechanical transcode is ffmpeg-processing; clipcannon and open-montage are editorial.

cases.prompt: Cut a highlight reel out of this two-hour recording, caption it, and render a vertical version for Reels.
cases.rationale: Editing existing footage into platform renders is clipcannon's stated scope against ffmpeg's mechanical one.

cases.prompt: Make a five-minute explainer video for this repository aimed at a non-technical buyer, with narration and captions.
cases.rationale: Repository-grounded audience video is codebase-video; open-montage is the general video producer with no repo grounding.

cases.prompt: Animate how the HNSW graph is traversed during a nearest-neighbour search — precise, mathematical, as a short clip.
cases.rationale: A mechanism that needs precise motion is manim; the video skills assemble rather than animate.

cases.prompt: Model a hard-surface drone chassis in Blender with PBR materials and give me a GPU render of it.
cases.rationale: Hard-surface modelling, materials and GPU render name blender directly.

cases.prompt: Implement double-jump with coyote time in my Godot 4 project. Just that one mechanic, not a whole studio.
cases.rationale: A targeted single mechanic without the 48-agent studio is godot-development's explicit boundary against game-dev.

cases.prompt: Train a Gaussian splat from this COLMAP capture, clean it up in the viewer and export the scene.
cases.rationale: 3DGS training, editing and export is lichtfeld-studio; spark-scene is the annotated-viewer neighbour.

cases.prompt: Where are my tokens going? I keep hitting plan limits and I think something automated is looping overnight.
cases.rationale: "Where are my tokens going" plus a suspected runaway daemon is token-audit verbatim; cost-estimation prices endpoints instead.

cases.prompt: Price up what it would cost to run this image-generation endpoint for a month, with the estimate-hold-settle flow.
cases.rationale: Endpoint cost tiers and the job lifecycle are cost-estimation, not local transcript accounting.

cases.prompt: Trace every caller of resolveEnabled across this nine-hundred-file repo and tell me the blast radius of changing its signature.
cases.rationale: Call-graph tracing and diff blast radius on a large codebase is codebase-memory's headline capability.

cases.prompt: I have a PRD. Generate the full documentation set from it — specs, ADRs, DDD files, task breakdown.
cases.rationale: PRD to complete documentation is phase 1 of the methodology ladder; build-with-quality is phase 3.

cases.prompt: This refactor touches the API, the client and the migration scripts. I want coverage and quality gates on it, not a cowboy job.
cases.rationale: Multi-file feature or refactor needing gates and coverage is build-with-quality's stated trigger.

cases.prompt: Take this from specification through pseudocode, architecture and refinement to completion, phase by phase.
cases.rationale: The five named SPARC phases are unambiguous once they are spelled out.

cases.prompt: Run an OWASP Top 10 pass over our REST API — auth, authorisation, dependency CVEs and secrets.
cases.rationale: Application-layer security testing is explicitly separated from Linux hardening in the skill's own description.

cases.prompt: Harden this Ubuntu box to the CIS benchmark and tell me where we stand on SOC2 compliance.
cases.rationale: Linux hardening and compliance is defense-security, the other half of the same explicit split.

cases.prompt: Stamp our signature PNG onto the bottom right of this PDF invoice. It just needs to look signed for the client.
cases.rationale: pdf-signing's description names this as its NOT case — stamping a signature image is imagemagick.

cases.prompt: Our counterparty requires a cryptographically signed, RFC-3161 timestamped PDF contract with a visible signature panel.
cases.rationale: PAdES signing with a visible panel and timestamping is the real pdf-signing case, paired with the imagemagick boundary above.

cases.prompt: Did anyone email me an invoice from Hetzner last month? Have a look through my mail.
cases.rationale: Invoices in the owner's personal email is email-search's quoted trigger.

cases.prompt: Check my work calendar for Thursday and send a reply on the client thread confirming the time.
cases.rationale: email-search's description excludes work mail, calendar and sending outright, and nothing else covers it — the correct answer is to decline, not to pick the nearest mail-shaped skill.

cases.prompt: I need to carry variables between steps while I work through this multi-stage numerical analysis interactively.
cases.rationale: State persisting across tool calls in a kernel is codeact's stated case.

cases.prompt: Knock out a quick one-shot Python script that renames these files by their EXIF date.
cases.rationale: codeact's description names one-shot scripts as its NOT case; a plain edit handles this, so the honest answer is none.

cases.prompt: This parser has to be right first time. Generate several candidates, execute each against the assertions, and keep the one that passes.
cases.rationale: Execution-gated branching generation where one attempt is insufficient is tree-search-coder's explicit scope.

cases.prompt: Replace this prompt-and-parse moderation step with a typed decision my code can branch on — TypeSafe Jev style, with a probability distribution.
cases.rationale: A typed Choice/Score/Noul primitive replacing prompt-and-parse, or TypeSafe named directly, is system-one.

cases.prompt: Clean the LLM fingerprints out of this article — em-dashes everywhere, hollow openers, and it reads like slop.
cases.rationale: Removing LLM writing tells from public-facing prose is prose-sanitiser; docs-alignment audits a corpus for accuracy instead.

cases.prompt: Audit our docs tree against the actual codebase and tell me what's stale, against the Diataxis quadrants.
cases.rationale: Corpus validation against code under Diataxis is docs-alignment, the accuracy half of the prose pair.

cases.prompt: Write a new skill for our internal deployment runbook, with proper frontmatter and progressive disclosure.
cases.rationale: Authoring a new skill is skill-builder; skill-tuning optimises one that already exists.

cases.prompt: Our diagrams skill picks the wrong output format half the time. Optimise its description against a measurable score with a held-out A/B.
cases.rationale: Raising a skill's success rate by evidence on a scoreable task is skill-tuning's stated boundary against eyeballing prose.

cases.prompt: Write a fused layernorm CUDA kernel and profile it against the cuBLAS baseline on this GPU.
cases.rationale: Custom kernel development and GPU profiling is cuda; pytorch-ml trains models with existing kernels.

cases.prompt: Set up distributed PyTorch training for this model across the two GPUs, with mixed precision.
cases.rationale: Distributed deep-learning training is pytorch-ml, the other half of the cuda pair.

cases.prompt: My Leptos app has a hydration mismatch on the dashboard route and the ssr feature build is broken.
cases.rationale: Hydration mismatch and ssr/hydrate build breaks are named in leptos's description; rust-development is the generic neighbour.

cases.prompt: Port this Python CLI to Rust, clippy and rustfmt clean, cross-compiled for musl.
cases.rationale: Cargo, clippy, cross-compilation on a CLI is rust-development's scope with no web framework involved.

cases.prompt: Assess this parcel in Lincolnshire for a ground-mounted solar farm — tilt, row spacing, yield and DNO feasibility.
cases.rationale: UK utility-scale PV siting composes qgis and blender but is its own skill.

cases.prompt: Reproject these shapefiles to EPSG:27700 and render a styled map with the layers ordered properly.
cases.rationale: CRS transforms, layer management and rendering are plain GIS operations.

cases.prompt: Do an SEO audit on the marketing site: Search Console, keyword research, schema markup and meta tags.
cases.rationale: Traditional SEO is toprank; bencium-aeo covers AI-search citation visibility instead.

cases.prompt: I'm writing against Next.js 15 and your API knowledge is stale. Pull the current documentation before you write anything.
cases.rationale: Version-specific library documentation to avoid stale-training hallucination is context7's whole purpose.

cases.prompt: Is the nightly dream loop still paused? Tell me what happened last night and what's in the inbox.
cases.rationale: Dream-engine status, pause state and inbox triage are dream-machine; the phrasing avoids a slash command, which the router skips.

cases.prompt: Set up a recurring agent task that runs at 3am every night and reports in the morning.
cases.rationale: Cron-style recurring agent tasks are hermes-scheduler; hooks-automation is event-driven rather than scheduled.

cases.prompt: Write the LaTeX for a Beamer deck with BibTeX references for the conference next month.
cases.rationale: Beamer and BibTeX are latex-documents; latex-book is deprecated and book-publishing is a whole manuscript.

cases.prompt: Turn this markdown manuscript into a print-ready and arXiv-ready book PDF with the figures redrawn.
cases.rationale: End-to-end book pipeline to KDP/arXiv is book-publishing, and it is the stated replacement for the deprecated latex-book.

cases.prompt: Spin up a mesh swarm of researcher agents with fault tolerance to work through this investigation in parallel.
cases.rationale: Mesh topology and fault tolerance for parallel local work is swarm-advanced; hive-mind is for consensus.

cases.prompt: I want the agents to reach Byzantine consensus on the design before any of them commit to code.
cases.rationale: Consensus-driven decisions with a queen-led hierarchy is hive-mind-advanced, the other half of the swarm pair.

cases.prompt: yes, that looks right — go ahead and apply it to the other two files as well
cases.rationale: Approval of work already in progress. The `none` rubric names follow-ups on in-session work explicitly.

cases.prompt: Thanks, that worked. What was the actual cause in the end?
cases.rationale: A conversational follow-up about work just done; no skill changes how it is answered.

cases.prompt: Can you re-run that command and show me the full output this time, not the tail?
cases.rationale: A re-run request. Naming a tooling skill here would inject advice the turn cannot use.

cases.prompt: No, I meant the other file — the one under tests, not the one in src.
cases.rationale: A clarification of a previous instruction; the `none` rubric lists clarifications first.

cases.prompt: Carry on with what you were doing, I just wanted to check in on progress.
cases.rationale: A check-in with no new task. A plausible pick here would be a false positive on an idle turn.

cases.prompt: Rename the variable foo to candidateCount everywhere in this one file, nothing else.
cases.rationale: A trivial edit, named in the `none` rubric. build-with-quality is the tempting wrong pick and is explicitly scoped to multi-file work.

cases.prompt: Why did that test fail? Just read the stack trace and tell me what it says.
cases.rationale: Reading one stack trace is ordinary assistant work; no skill's guidance would change the answer.

cases.prompt: Undo that last edit please, it broke the build and I want to think again.
cases.rationale: A revert request on in-session work. agentic-jujutsu is the tempting wrong pick but is about multi-agent concurrent VCS.

cases.prompt: Give me a one-line summary of what you just changed so I can put it in the commit.
cases.rationale: A summary of the session's own work; prose-sanitiser is the tempting wrong pick and is for public-facing prose.

cases.prompt: Commit what we've got with a sensible message and push it to the branch.
cases.rationale: Plain git work. The github-* skills are about PRs, releases, boards and Actions, not a local commit.

cases.prompt: Is 0.74 a reasonable confidence for a classifier, generally speaking? Just curious.
cases.rationale: A general knowledge question. system-one is the tempting wrong pick because of the word confidence, but nothing is being built.

cases.prompt: Explain what a monad is in two sentences, no code, I'm on my phone.
cases.rationale: explainer is the tempting wrong pick; it is scoped to explaining a repo or product, not a general concept.

cases.prompt: Let's pause here for the night. Pick it up tomorrow from where we left off.
cases.rationale: Session housekeeping. lazy-fetch is the tempting wrong pick — it is the single most over-fired skill in the real log (9 of 99 routes).

cases.prompt: What time is it in Tokyo right now, roughly? I need to book a call.
cases.rationale: A trivial factual question with no repo, no artefact and no tool that changes the answer.
